claim: An applicant must clearly state in its application that, in accordance with the design plans submitted with the application to the Board, it shall invest not less than the required capital under the article into the gaming facility.
reason: Statutory minimum license threshold: the applicant must state it will invest at least the required capital in the facility, a concrete duty tied to project delivery.

claim: An applicant must clearly state in its application that it shall own or acquire, within sixty days after a license has been awarded, the land where the gaming facility is proposed to be constructed, provided that ownership of the land may include a tenancy for a term of years under a lease extending not less than sixty years beyond the term of the gaming license.
reason: Statutory minimum license threshold: the applicant must obtain qualifying land control within 60 days of award, with a lease allowed only if it runs 60 years beyond the license term.

claim: If a License is issued, the contents of this RFA, any modifications thereof made by the Board, and the respective Application and any changes thereto approved by the State will become obligations of the Gaming Facility licensee.
reason: Sentence 167 is an omnibus incorporation clause: it says the RFA, later modifications, and the application become obligations if licensed, but it does not itself identify a distinct concrete duty or outcome the public could separately track.

claim: Pursuant to PML Section 1321-j, the Board shall conduct an analysis of the revenue impact of each Applicant’s proposed gaming facility on existing facilities and potential facilities.
reason: This is a Board review activity in the award process: the Board must conduct a revenue-impact analysis of each proposal before selection.

claim: Prior to any public presentations, the Board will post to nycasinos.ny.gov the rules and procedures relating to the conduct of such presentations.
reason: Posting presentation rules and procedures is a solicitation/public-presentation mechanic, not a project delivery commitment.

organization: Applicants and their agents and representatives
claim: If the Board convenes a public hearing during Stage 2, Applicants and their agents and representatives are required to attend the hearing, and may make a presentation and respond to questions of the Board or public comments as directed by the Board or the Board’s designee.
reason: It states a Stage 2 hearing attendance requirement tied to the RFA review process, not a project delivery commitment.

claim: Each Applicant must have at least one individual available who, based on actual knowledge, is prepared to respond on behalf of the Applicant to reasonably anticipated questions or public comments regarding its Application and/or Supplement, including the scope and quality of the proposed gaming area and amenities, the integration of the proposed Gaming Facility into the community and nearby municipalities, and the extent of required mitigation plans.
reason: This is an application-stage requirement to have a knowledgeable representative available to answer hearing questions.

claim: Before any such public hearing, the Board will prescribe on its website the manner in which it will receive comments from members of the public.
reason: It describes how the Board will run the public-hearing comment process on the website.

claim: During the Restricted Period, an Applicant is restricted from making contacts with anyone at the Commission or the Board other than designees of the Commission’s staff.
reason: This is a communication restriction during the Restricted Period in the application process.

organization: Each lobbyist seeking to engage in lobbying activity on behalf of a client or a client's interest before the Commission
claim: Each lobbyist seeking to engage in lobbying activity on behalf of a client or a client's interest before the Commission shall first register with the secretary of the Commission, in addition to any other registration and reporting required by law.
reason: It is a general legal registration requirement for lobbyists before the Commission, not a project-specific deliverable or benefit.

claim: The secretary shall cause a lobbyist registration to be available on the Commission's website within five days of submission.
reason: This is an administrative website-posting duty for lobbyist registrations, not a project outcome or project-accountability term.

claim: Each Applicant has a continuing duty to disclose to the Board promptly, in writing and electronically, any changes or updates to the information submitted in its Application, including the Supplement, or any related materials submitted in connection therewith.
reason: It requires applicants to update application materials during the RFA process.

claim: By submitting an Application, an Applicant warrants, under penalty of perjury, that its Application was arrived at independently and without collusion aimed at restricting competition.
reason: This is a bid-submission certification against collusion, part of the solicitation mechanics.

claim: No results of the Board’s selection process may be released by Applicants without prior approval by the Board and then only to persons and entities designated by the Board.
reason: Sentence 265 does not say Applicants are the ones barred from releasing results; the claim adds that actor.

claim: The Board reserves the authority to waive any requirement of this RFA that is not prescribed by the Act, or any defects of any Applications, if in the judgment of the Board such waiver is deemed by the Board to further the policy objectives of the PML Article 13.
reason: A reserved solicitation power to waive certain RFA requirements or application defects; it governs how the award process may be run, not a deliverable to the public.

claim: The Board reserves the authority to eliminate any non-mandatory specification(s) that cannot be complied with by any of the Applicants.
reason: This is the Board’s discretion to remove non-mandatory specifications in the RFA process, not a project outcome or public-facing obligation.

claim: The Board reserves the authority to amend the RFA and direct Applicants to submit modifications to their Applications accordingly.
reason: Amending the RFA and requiring application modifications is a procurement/process step for applicants.

claim: The Board reserves the authority to change any of the scheduled dates stated in this RFA.
reason: Changing scheduled RFA dates is purely about the application timetable.

claim: The Board reserves the authority to reject any or all Applications received in response to this RFA, and reissue a modified version of this RFA.
reason: Rejecting applications and reissuing a modified RFA is a solicitation decision about how the competition proceeds.

claim: The Board reserves the authority to withdraw the RFA at any time, at the sole discretion of the Board.
reason: Withdrawing the RFA is a process-level discretion over the solicitation, not a promised project action.

claim: The Board reserves the authority to seek clarifications and revisions to Applications.
reason: Seeking clarifications and revisions concerns evaluation of applications during the award process.

claim: The Board reserves the authority to use information obtained through site visits, management interviews, the State’s investigation of an Applicant’s qualifications, experience, ability or financial standing, and materials or information submitted by the Applicant in response to requests for clarifying information in the course of evaluation and/or selection under this RFA or otherwise.
reason: Using information from interviews, investigations, site visits, and clarification materials describes evaluation inputs for selecting applicants.

claim: The Board reserves the authority to disqualify any Applicant whose conduct and/or Applications fail to conform to the requirements of this RFA.
reason: Disqualifying nonconforming applicants is an enforcement step within the RFA process.

organization: the Board and its representatives and designees
claim: The Board and its representatives and designees shall have the right, in their discretion, to use or consider any information provided or disclosed anywhere in an Application or otherwise provided by an Applicant or Operator for any purpose under the PML notwithstanding the heading, section or item of this RFA to which such information may respond or its apparent relevance, or lack thereof, to any other heading, section or item.
reason: It gives the Board discretion to consider information anywhere in an application for any PML purpose; this is an application-review rule.

claim: Upon both Return Dates, the Board will publicly announce the entities have submitted Applications and/or Supplements.
reason: The Board will announce which entities submitted applications/supplements after the return dates; this is a concrete public step in the licensing process.

claim: Applications, Supplements and associated materials will be treated as public records and, as soon as possible after both Return Dates, will be posted online for public review, with redactions of language exempt from disclosure pursuant to New York State’s Freedom of Information Law (FOIL).
reason: It imposes a concrete public-disclosure duty: application materials will be treated as public records and posted online, subject to FOIL redactions.

organization: The Board, Commission staff, and the CAC
claim: Unredacted portions of Applications, Supplements, and associated materials will remain confidential as may be required by statute and reviewed by the Board, Commission staff, and the CAC.
reason: Sets submission/disclosure handling for application materials: unredacted portions stay confidential for review by the Board, Commission staff, and CAC.

organization: Each Applicant, Operator, and direct or indirect owner of an Applicant or Operator
claim: As a condition to submitting an Application, each Applicant, Operator, and direct or indirect owner of an Applicant or Operator shall execute and submit a State Waiver under which, on its own behalf and on behalf of specified related persons, it releases, waives, covenants not to sue or make any claim for damages, costs, fees, expenses, or any relief whatsoever, agrees not to seek any appeal, review, or reconsideration of any decision of the State, the Commission, and the Board, and indemnifies, defends, and holds them harmless.
reason: A required waiver and indemnification is an application prerequisite, not a project delivery commitment.
adjudicated_wording: As a condition of submitting an application, each applicant, operator, and direct or indirect owner of an applicant or operator must execute and submit a State Waiver under which it releases, waives, covenants not to sue or make claims for damages or other relief, agrees not to seek appeal, review, or reconsideration of decisions of the State, the Commission, and the Board, and agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold them harmless, as more specifically described in the State Waiver.

organization: Each Applicant, Operator, and direct or indirect owner of an Applicant or Operator
claim: As a condition to submitting an Application, each Applicant, Operator, and direct or indirect owner of an Applicant or Operator shall execute and deliver a Section 1311 Waiver under which, on its own behalf and on behalf of specified related persons, it releases, waives, covenants not to sue or make any claim for damages, costs, fees, expenses, or any relief whatsoever regarding any rights to bring an action to recover a fee pursuant to PML Section 1311, and indemnifies, defends, and holds harmless the State, the Commission, the Board, their officials, agents, consultants, and representatives, and any Gaming Facility licensee.
reason: This Section 1311 waiver is another mandatory application-submission condition about legal rights, not a public-facing project outcome.
adjudicated_wording: As a condition of submitting an application, each applicant, operator, and direct or indirect owner of an applicant or operator must execute and deliver a Section 1311 Waiver under which it releases, waives, covenants not to sue or make claims for damages or other relief regarding any right to bring an action to recover a fee under PML Section 1311, and agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the State, the Commission, the Board, their officials, agents, consultants, and representatives, and any gaming facility licensee, as more specifically described in the Section 1311 Waiver.

organization: The Commission or the Commission’s designated agents
claim: The Commission or the Commission’s designated agents shall subject all Applicants for a License and each Related Party to a thorough background investigation into the suitability of those persons and entities.
reason: Describes the Commission’s required suitability background investigation of applicants and related parties as part of license review.
adjudicated_wording: All applicants for a license, and each related party, shall be subject to a thorough background investigation into suitability by the Commission or the Commission’s designated agents.

claim: Each Applicant and Related Party must prove by clear and convincing evidence its suitability and qualifications to hold a License or otherwise be qualified within the meaning of PML Article 13.
reason: Sets the evidentiary standard applicants and related parties must meet to qualify for a license in the application process.
adjudicated_wording: Each Applicant and Related Party must prove by clear and convincing evidence its suitability and qualifications to hold a License or otherwise be qualified within the meaning of PML Article 13.

claim: In conducting the suitability investigation pursuant to PML Section 1317, the Commission shall consider the Applicant’s overall reputation, including the Applicant’s integrity, honesty, good character and reputation; financial stability, integrity and background; business practices and ability to establish and maintain a successful Gaming Facility; history of compliance with gaming licensing requirements in other jurisdictions; whether the Applicant is a defendant in litigation involving its business practices at the time of Application; the suitability of all parties in interest to the License, including Affiliates and Close Associates, and the Applicant’s financial resources; and whether the Applicant is disqualified pursuant to PML Section 1318 from receiving a License.
reason: Lists factors the Commission must consider in suitability review; these are licensing evaluation criteria, not promised project outcomes or adopted community-benefit conditions.

claim: In considering the rehabilitation of an applicant for a gaming facility license, the Commission shall not automatically disqualify an applicant if the applicant affirmatively demonstrates, by clear and convincing evidence, that the applicant has financial responsibility, character, reputation, integrity and general fitness to warrant belief by the Commission that the applicant will act honestly, fairly, soundly and efficiently as a gaming licensee.
reason: Binds the Commission not to automatically disqualify a rehabilitated applicant if the applicant proves the listed fitness factors by clear and convincing evidence.

claim: The New York State Police will conduct the background investigations.
reason: Describes who performs background investigations as part of the license review process, not a project deliverable.

claim: An Applicant shall make a good faith effort to determine whether it and its respective related parties must submit background investigation forms as set forth in this section.
reason: Requires the applicant to determine which related parties must file background forms; this is an application filing step.

claim: If the Board determines that an Applicant has failed to provide background forms for a person or entity required to disclose, the Board will afford the Applicant the opportunity to submit promptly the necessary background forms for that person or entity.
reason: Commits the Board to give an applicant a chance to cure missing background-form submissions during review.

organization: Each Applicant and its respective Related Parties
claim: On the Return Date, each Applicant and its respective Related Parties shall submit the listed background-investigation materials.
reason: Sets a filing requirement on the return date for applicants and related parties to submit background-investigation materials.

claim: The Commission or the Board, in their sole discretion and as applicable to their respective duties under PML Article 13, shall determine the persons and entities qualifying as the Applicant and any Related Parties, including whether to grant temporary or permanent exemptions for particular persons or entities such as certain institutional investors, passive investors, stockholders of publicly held corporations or other circumstances.
reason: Gives the Commission or Board discretion to decide who counts as the applicant or related parties and whether exemptions apply in the licensing process.

claim: If, after review of an Applicant’s Application and related Background Investigation Forms, the Commission determines that persons or entities are Related Parties but have not filed the appropriate Background Investigation Forms, the Commission may require those persons or entities to file the appropriate Background Investigation Form within a time period designated by the Commission.
reason: This gives the Commission discretion during application review to require missing background forms from related parties; it is a licensing-process mechanic, not a tracked project or public-benefit commitment.

claim: Applicants are obligated to establish their suitability for a License and the suitability of all Related Parties by clear and convincing evidence.
reason: This is the applicant’s evidentiary burden to prove suitability for a license, which is part of the award process rather than a concrete deliverable or project duty.
adjudicated_wording: Applicants are obligated to establish their suitability for a License and the suitability of all Related Parties by clear and convincing evidence.

claim: Each Applicant is required to submit Background Investigation Forms for, among others, persons having a beneficial or proprietary interest of 5 percent or more in an Applicant or Operator.
reason: This is a filing requirement in the application process: applicants must submit background forms for 5% owners and similar parties.

claim: The Commission and Board reserve the right to require submission of Background Investigation Forms for, and investigate the suitability of, any other Affiliate, Close Associate or Financing Source of the Applicant, beyond the initial 5-percent beneficial-or-proprietary-interest threshold, as they may determine in their discretion.
reason: This reserves agency discretion to demand more background forms and suitability review beyond the 5% threshold, which is a process/eligibility provision.

claim: The $1 million Application fee shall be used, in part, to defray the costs associated with processing the Application and investigating the Applicant and Related Parties, and related costs.
reason: This specifically governs how the $1 million application fee must be used to cover application-processing and investigation costs, a concrete public-money condition.

claim: If the allocable costs of processing the Application, investigating the Applicant and Related Parties, and other uses of the application fee set forth in PML Section 1321-d(2)(c) exceed the initial application fee, the Applicant shall pay the additional amount to the Commission within 30 days after notification of insufficient funds.
reason: This imposes a concrete duty on the applicant to pay additional investigation/application costs within 30 days if the initial fee is insufficient.

claim: If an additional amount is paid to the Commission for those costs and the costs do not exceed the amount remitted, the Commission shall return any unexpended portion of that additional amount to the Applicant.
reason: This creates a concrete refund obligation: if extra funds were paid and not fully used, the unexpended portion must be returned to the applicant.

claim: The Applicant must meet or exceed a Minimum Capital Investment of $500 million for its Gaming Facility.
reason: The RFA sets a binding minimum: the Applicant must demonstrate its Gaming Facility meets or exceeds a $500 million minimum capital investment.

claim: Prior to official review by the Board, each potential license Applicant must demonstrate public support via a vote by an applicable CAC established pursuant to PML Section 1321-d(3).
reason: A pre-review application prerequisite: an applicant must obtain CAC public-support approval before the Board will officially review the application.

claim: The CAC must conduct all meetings under the open meetings provisions contained in Article 7 of the Public Officers Law.
reason: This is a procedural rule for the CAC’s meetings during the license review process, not a project delivery commitment.

claim: The CAC must review, solicit public comments and written submissions of such comments, and hold public hearings.
reason: These are CAC hearing and comment-process duties for reviewing an application, fitting review mechanics rather than a project outcome.

claim: Upon a two-thirds vote, the CAC must issue a finding either establishing public support approving or disapproving the application.
reason: This is a CAC decision step in the approval process: after a two-thirds vote it must issue a support or disapproval finding.

claim: Prior to official review by the Board, each potential license Applicant must prove compliance with all State and local zoning requirements, as set forth in PML Section 1321-k.
reason: Proving zoning compliance is a prerequisite for official Board review, so it is an application-review requirement.

claim: On the Return Date, an Applicant must waive all rights it or any affiliated entity possess under PML Section 1311 to bring an action to recover a fee.
reason: Waiving rights under PML 1311 is a filing/eligibility condition attached to the application process.

claim: On the Return Date, each Applicant is required to pay to the Commission an initial Application fee of $1 million, concurrently with the submission of an Application, to defray processing, CAC-related Commission expenses, and investigation costs.
reason: The $1 million payment is an application fee due with submission; it governs how an application is processed, not project delivery.

claim: If the costs of processing, Commission expenses, investigation and related costs exceed the initial Application fee, the Applicant shall pay the additional amount to the Commission within 30 days after notification of insufficient fees or the Application shall be rejected.
reason: This is a fee-processing rule: if review costs exceed the initial fee, the applicant must pay the balance within 30 days or face rejection.

claim: If the costs of investigation and expenses do not exceed the fee remitted, the Commission shall return any unexpended portion to the Applicant, as required by PML Section 1321-d(2)(c).
reason: Returning any unused application-fee balance is part of fee administration for the licensing process.

claim: For all Applicants that receive approval from the applicable CAC and for local land use, the Board shall evaluate the proposals based on the criteria set forth in PML Section 1321-j.
reason: It describes how the Board will evaluate eligible proposals under statutory criteria, which is review procedure.

claim: In recommending an Applicant for license, the Board is required to evaluate and determine which Applicant or Applicants proposes to best advance the objectives listed under each technical factor.
reason: This states the Board’s evaluative task in recommending licensees; it is a decision standard, not a project promise.

claim: The Board shall conduct an analysis of the revenue impact of each Applicant’s proposed gaming facilities on existing facilities and potential new facilities.
reason: The Board’s revenue-impact analysis is a review activity performed during the selection process.

claim: If the Applicant receives a gaming license, the Applicant's prospective capital investments to be summarized for the Board include remediation of environmental conditions or hazardous materials.
reason: The text requires applicants to submit a capital-investment summary that includes remediation; it does not obligate them to perform remediation.

claim: The Applicant is to make a commitment to hire a minimum number of employees, both full-time and part-time, at the opening of the Gaming Facility, as part of providing a high number of quality jobs in the Gaming Facility.
reason: Sentence 636 requires the applicant to submit a description of its commitment to hire a minimum number of employees; it is an application submission requirement, not itself an executed or regulator-imposed hiring obligation.

claim: The Applicant is to set out minimum commitments, expressed in terms of annual biddable spend, for the use of New York-based suppliers and materials in both the construction and furniture, fixtures, and equipment furnishing phase of the project and in the operational phase of the project.
reason: Sentence 641 requires the applicant to describe plans and minimum commitments for New York-based suppliers/materials in the application; the text is about what must be submitted, not a standalone adopted project commitment.

claim: During construction, a licensee shall provide regular updates to the Commission to document improvements to the facility design.
reason: Sentence 731 imposes an ongoing duty on any licensee during construction to provide regular design-update reports to the Commission.

claim: Changes to the initial design that reduce the size, quality, or fit and finish of a facility will not be permitted, because the Application will be evaluated and approved based on the initial design.
reason: Sentence 732 sets a concrete restriction on the approved project: post-approval design changes that reduce size, quality, or fit and finish are not allowed.
adjudicated_wording: Because the application will be evaluated and approved based on the initial design, a licensee may not make changes that reduce the size, quality, or fit and finish of the facility.

claim: An Application is for one Gaming Facility, and if an Applicant’s property comprises two non-contiguous parcels, gaming will be allowed on only one parcel.
reason: This sets solicitation/project-site rules for what an application may cover—one gaming facility, and gaming on only one of two non-contiguous parcels—not a promised public delivery.

claim: Pursuant to PML Section 1316 (as incorporated by PML Section 1321-f), the Applicant must own or acquire the land where the Gaming Facility is proposed to be constructed within 60 days after a License has been awarded; an Applicant is deemed to own the land if it has entered into a tenancy for a term of years under a lease that extends not less than 60 years beyond 10 years for a License.
reason: This is a concrete post-award duty: the applicant must own or acquire the project land within 60 days after license award, with a specific lease-based ownership standard.

organization: Applicant or, if applicable, the Operator, or its Affiliates
claim: The Applicant or, if applicable, the Operator, or its Affiliates is prepared to provide to the Commission, over and above the deposit or bond required by PML Section 1321-e(1), financial commitments and guarantees to ensure that the Gaming Facility is completed, license conditions are fulfilled, and sufficient working capital is available to allow continuous operation in the manner described in the Applicant’s financial forecasts, including commitments such as letters of credit, construction completion guaranties, performance bonds, keep-well agreements, MOUs or other agreements or commitments in connection with the Gaming Facility.
reason: These sentences require the applicant to submit a description and examples of guarantees it is prepared to offer; they do not themselves impose or confirm a specific guarantee that must later be delivered.

claim: The Applicant must describe its commitments to mitigate the proposed Gaming Facility’s construction and operating impacts on each host community and nearby municipalities, including traffic mitigation, infrastructure costs, increased emergency-service costs, and the other impacts identified in the RFA studies, and provide any contracts, agreements, or other understandings evidencing those mitigation commitments.
reason: RFA submission requirement to describe mitigation commitments and submit supporting agreements; it does not itself obligate the applicant to carry out specific mitigation.

claim: The Applicant must describe the measures that will be taken to mitigate all construction impacts on the local community, including anticipated street and sidewalk closures, traffic redirection, impacts on existing parking, noise and dust impacts, and plans for mitigating those impacts during and following construction.
reason: This is an application instruction to describe construction-impact mitigation measures, closures, traffic redirection, and related plans, not an adopted duty to implement them.

claim: The Applicant must present its plans and commitments to remedy or mitigate any negative housing impacts in each host community and nearby municipalities resulting from new jobs provided by the Gaming Facility, and provide any contracts, agreements, or other understandings evidencing those mitigation commitments.
reason: The text requires the applicant to present housing-mitigation plans and commitments and provide supporting documents, but it does not impose a concrete mitigation obligation in this passage.

claim: The Applicant must present its plans and commitments to remedy or mitigate any negative impacts on school populations in the host community and nearby municipalities resulting from new jobs provided by the Gaming Facility, including impacts relating to after-school programs, childcare programs, and demographic effects, and provide any contracts, agreements, or other understandings evidencing those mitigation commitments.
reason: This is a requirement to describe school-impact mitigation plans and submit any supporting agreements, not a binding project condition to deliver those measures.

claim: The Applicant must describe measures to mitigate the impact of the facility on underserved communities, including examples of such work in other locations.
reason: The applicant is asked to describe measures to mitigate impacts on underserved communities; that is a submission requirement, not a promised outcome.

claim: The Applicant must identify the metrics and/or milestones it will use to measure the facility’s impact on the community and state what remediation steps it will take if those metrics are not met.
reason: The RFA requires the applicant to identify metrics and remediation steps in its application, but does not itself commit the applicant to those steps.

claim: The Applicant must describe plans for promoting local businesses in the host community and nearby municipalities, including developing cross-marketing strategies with local restaurants, small businesses, hotels, and retail facilities, and including any plans for coordination with local tourism-promotion entities.
reason: This calls for a description of plans to promote local businesses and coordinate with tourism entities; it is solicitation content, not a concrete public commitment to execute.

claim: The Applicant must describe plans for contracting with local business owners to provide goods and services to the Gaming Facility, including plans designed to assist businesses in the State in identifying the Gaming Facility’s goods-and-services needs.
reason: The applicant must describe plans for contracting with local businesses and helping state businesses identify needs; this is an application-content requirement, not an executed commitment.

claim: The Applicant must provide local agreements designed to expand the Gaming Facility’s draw, meaning the number of patrons brought to the Region.
reason: The passage requires submission of local agreements designed to expand patron draw as part of the application; it does not report a specific agreement or impose a standalone delivery obligation.

claim: The Applicant must describe plans for cross-marketing with other attractions and provide any contracts, agreements, or other understandings evidencing that cross-marketing commitment.
reason: This is a requirement to describe cross-marketing plans and provide any supporting agreements, not a specific executed partnership or binding duty to carry out cross-marketing.

claim: The Applicant is to propose baseline and improved building design elements and measures for its Gaming Facility to become certified under a certification category in the Leadership in Environmental and Energy Design (LEED) program created by the United States Green Building Council.
reason: Sentence 990 requires the applicant to submit a description of proposed LEED design elements; it is an application submission, not a binding commitment to achieve certification.

claim: The Applicant is to propose steps, plans and measures, including infrastructure improvements, to mitigate traffic flow and vehicle trips in the vicinity of the Gaming Facility, including plans to use public or alternate transportation methods and transportation demand management.
reason: Sentences 991-992 ask for a description of traffic-mitigation and transportation plans to include in the application, not a duty to carry them out.

claim: The Applicant is to propose efforts to conserve water and manage storm water at the Gaming Facility, including storm-water management plans and water-efficiency and conservation measures such as low-flow fixtures, water-efficient appliances and water conservation implementation.
reason: Sentences 993-995 require a description of planned water and storm-water measures; they are application materials, not promised implementation.

claim: The Applicant is to propose ensuring the use of Energy Star-rated equipment and high-efficiency HVAC equipment and appliances throughout the Gaming Facility complex.
reason: Sentence 996 asks for a description of plans to ensure Energy Star and high-efficiency equipment use; this is a proposal requirement, not an executed obligation.

claim: The Applicant is to propose procuring or generating on-site at least 10 percent of the facility's annual electricity consumption from renewable energy sources qualified by the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA).
reason: Sentence 997 requires a description of plans for at least 10% renewable electricity; the 10% figure is part of the plan to be submitted, not a standalone commitment in the text.

claim: The Applicant is to propose developing an ongoing system that will submeter and monitor all major sources of energy consumption and undertaking regular and sustained efforts throughout the life cycle of the facility to maintain and improve energy efficiency and reliance on renewable sources of power in all buildings and equipment that are part of the facility.
reason: Sentence 998 asks for a description of plans for submeters, monitoring, and ongoing efficiency efforts; it is an application requirement rather than a promised outcome.

claim: The gaming facility will comply with applicable local laws regulating energy efficiency, such as New York City Local Law 97 of 2019, as amended.
reason: Sentence 999 only says to describe how the facility will comply with applicable energy-efficiency laws; the candidate turns that into an actual compliance commitment by the facility.

claim: The Applicant is to propose establishing, funding and maintaining human resource hiring and training practices at the proposed Gaming Facility that promote the development of a skilled and diverse workforce and access to promotion opportunities through a workforce training program that establishes transparent career paths with measurable criteria leading to increased responsibility and higher pay grades and designed to allow employees to pursue career advancement and promotion.
reason: Sentences 1001-1002 ask the applicant to explain how it proposes to establish workforce practices and career paths; this is proposal content, not a binding undertaking.

claim: The Applicant is to propose establishing, funding and maintaining human resource hiring and training practices at the proposed Gaming Facility through a workforce training program that provides employee access to additional resources, such as tuition reimbursement or stipend policies, to enable employees to acquire the education or job training needed to advance career paths based on increased responsibility and pay grades.
reason: Sentences 1001 and 1003 require the applicant to describe a proposed training program with resources like tuition reimbursement or stipends; it is not an executed promise to provide them.

claim: The Applicant is to propose establishing, funding and maintaining human resource hiring and training practices at the proposed Gaming Facility through a workforce training program that establishes an on-site child day care program.
reason: Sentences 1001 and 1004 ask how the applicant proposes a workforce program that includes an on-site child day care program; this remains a proposal requirement.

organization: Applicant and, as applicable, the Operator
claim: The Applicant and, as applicable, the Operator are to identify whether they plan to establish employee assistance programs, including those concerning substance abuse and problem gaming.
reason: Sentence 1005 requires identifying whether the applicant/operator plans to establish employee assistance programs; it is an application disclosure step, not a commitment to establish them.

organization: Applicant that has not entered into labor peace agreements
claim: If the Applicant has not entered into labor peace agreements with labor organizations actually engaged in representing gaming or hospitality industry workers in the State, the Applicant must state that it will enter into such labor peace agreements and maintain them in place during the term of a License.
reason: Sentence 1017 imposes a concrete if-applicable duty: an applicant without labor peace agreements must provide an instrument stating it will enter into them and keep them in force for the license term.

organization: Applicant and, as applicable, the Operator
claim: The Applicant and, as applicable, the Operator, must incorporate a program of equal opportunity by which the Applicant guarantees to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees qualified for licensure in all employment categories, including minorities, women and persons with disabilities.
reason: Sentence 1030 requires a submission describing how equal opportunity will be incorporated; the candidate turns that application-description requirement into a direct execution mandate.

claim: None of the proposal parameters submitted in the first submission, including but not limited to jobs, capital investment, and a gaming facility of the highest caliber, should be amended based on the tax rate selected by the Applicant.
reason: Sentence 1063 sets a specific proposal constraint: first-submission parameters such as jobs and capital investment are not to be changed based on the applicant’s selected tax rate.

organization: Applicant awarded a gaming facility license by the Commission
claim: Upon award of a gaming facility license, the Applicant must deposit no less than 5 and no more than 10 percent of the total investment proposed in the Application into an interest-bearing escrow account approved by the Commission.
reason: Concrete post-award duty: a license awardee must place 5-10% of proposed investment into Commission-approved escrow.

claim: The Commission will, by regulation, determine the deposit amount for the required escrow deposit.
reason: This assigns the Commission discretion to set the escrow percentage by regulation, rather than promising a project outcome.

claim: If the Applicant is unable to complete the Gaming Facility, the required deposit shall be forfeited to the State.
reason: Concrete enforcement term: if the facility is not completed, the deposit is forfeited to the State.
adjudicated_wording: If an applicant is unable to complete the Gaming Facility, the required deposit will be forfeited to the State.

claim: In place of a cash deposit, an Applicant may secure a deposit bond in a form acceptable to the Board ensuring that the deposit shall be forfeited to the State if the Applicant is unable to complete the Gaming Facility.
reason: Concrete alternative compliance path: the applicant may use an approved bond securing forfeiture if it cannot complete the facility.

claim: The Board has determined that the license fee will be $500 million.
reason: Sets a specific $500 million license fee, a concrete public-money term tied to licensure.

claim: Licensees must provide and satisfy all requests for information pertaining to qualification.

reason: Sentence 393 describes HRMP’s planned efforts and priorities, but gives no concrete threshold, date, or independently trackable deliverable.
adjudicated_wording: HRMP has planned efforts to hire local residents, procure products and services from local Queens merchants, and develop a diverse workforce while prioritizing hiring unemployed or underemployed people.

claim: HRMP plans significant investments in improving traffic and transit infrastructure and facilities, making the area safer for pedestrians and bikers, providing a large multi-use outdoor space, contributing to local social services and a community impact fund, and making the facility sustainable, resilient, and energy- and water-efficient.
reason: Sentence 394 attributes concrete project actions and contributions to HRMP—transport/transit improvements, safer pedestrian/bike access, outdoor space, social-service/community-fund support, and sustainability features.

claim: Resorts World proposes to convert and expand the existing video lottery terminal facility in Queens into a full commercial casino.
reason: Sentence 401 states the core project specification: converting and expanding the existing facility into a full commercial casino.

claim: Resorts World estimates total capital investment of $3.3 billion for the project.
reason: Sentence 402 gives a project-specific capital investment amount of $3.3 billion.

claim: Resorts World currently expects the converted facility to open in March 2026, with completion of the expansion in 2029 and full project completion in 2031.
reason: Sentence 403 provides attributable project timing: March 2026 opening, 2029 expansion completion, and 2031 full completion.

claim: Resorts World proposes a casino featuring at least 4,635 slot machines and 534 gaming tables.
reason: Sentence 405 sets specific gaming-capacity levels for the project: at least 4,635 slots and 534 tables.

claim: Resorts World proposes one new hotel and modification of an existing hotel for a total of 1,963 rooms, approximately 6 percent of which will be suites.
reason: Sentence 406 gives a concrete hotel program: 1,963 total rooms with about 6% suites.

claim: Resorts World proposes a 7,000-seat event center.
reason: Sentence 407 identifies a specific facility component with a measurable size: a 7,000-seat event center.

claim: Resorts World proposes a branded dayclub.
reason: Sentence 408 identifies a specific planned project component: a branded dayclub.

claim: Resorts World proposes more than 20 food and beverage outlets, including existing venues.
reason: Sentence 409 gives a concrete amenity count for the project: more than 20 food and beverage outlets.

claim: The Board recommends that Resorts World be licensed for 4,635 slot machines and 534 gaming tables rather than the higher numbers in its application, to ensure the quality of visitors’ experience.
reason: Sentence 416 is the Board recommending a lower licensed gaming-position cap than the application showed; it is a recommended licensing term, not an adopted one here.
adjudicated_wording: The Board recommends that Resorts World be licensed for 4,635 slot machines and 534 gaming tables, rather than the higher numbers referenced elsewhere in its application, to ensure the quality of visitors’ experience.

claim: Resorts World will renovate the existing Hyatt Regency and reduce it from 400 to 363 rooms, and will also construct a new 1,600-room Crockfords Hotel.
reason: Sentences 418-419 specify hotel reconfiguration and new construction: renovation/reduction of the existing Hyatt and a new 1,600-room Crockfords Hotel.

claim: Resorts World currently has $925 million in committed debt financing, contingent upon the issuance of a casino license, to fund the license fee and initial capital expenditures.
reason: Sentence 427 reports current contingent financing status, not a public-facing project deliverable, target, or duty owed to the public.
adjudicated_wording: Resorts World currently has $925 million in committed debt financing, contingent on issuance of a casino license, to fund the license fee and initial capital expenditures.

organization: Resorts World New York City and Genting Americas Inc.
claim: Resorts World and its North American parent, Genting Americas Inc., have committed individually and collectively to guarantee access to the capital necessary to complete the project.
reason: Sentence 431 says Resorts World and GAI committed to guarantee access to the capital needed to complete the project, a concrete completion-support commitment.

claim: Resorts World will contribute $500 million in license fees.
reason: Sentence 439 gives a specific project-related public payment amount: $500 million in license fees.

claim: Resorts World projects 4,543 FTE employees and a total headcount of 5,007 to operate the casino upon full buildout, with 56 percent of FTEs filled by Queens residents, and the Board stresses that Resorts World must meet these targets.
reason: Sentences 443 and 446 provide specific employment and local-hiring targets and say Resorts World must meet them.

claim: Resorts World must meet its permanent-employment diversity targets of 47 percent women, 85 percent minorities, and approximately 5 percent service-disabled veterans, because the Board treated those job-creation and diversity outcomes as key factors in its recommendation.
reason: Sentences 445-446 pair specific permanent-employment diversity targets with the Board’s statement that Resorts World “must meet these targets,” making this a concrete accountability duty.

claim: Resorts World has offered an annual commitment, for the duration of the license term, to a workforce housing fund equal to the lesser of 2 percent of incremental gross gaming revenue above 2025 levels or $25 million per year.
reason: Sentence 452 states an annual commitment by Resorts World, for the license term, to fund workforce housing at a defined formula and cap.

organization: the Commission and the elected officials represented on the Community Advisory Committee
claim: The Board urges the Commission and the elected officials represented on the Community Advisory Committee to monitor carefully the implementation of Resorts World’s workforce-housing-fund commitment.
reason: Sentence 455 is the Board urging public officials to monitor implementation; it is not a project delivery commitment or adopted condition imposed on Resorts World.

claim: Resorts World pledged an initial $50 million investment in the design and preconstruction programming of an Innovation Campus on the edge of Rockaway Boulevard, physically separate from the casino.
reason: Sentence 456 reports a specific pledged investment: an initial $50 million for design and preconstruction programming of the Innovation Campus.

claim: Resorts World pledged an annual commitment, for the duration of the license term, of the lesser of 2 percent of incremental gross gaming revenue above 2025 levels or $25 million per year to a community fund that would be separately and independently responsible for the actual construction, maintenance, and cooperation of the RW Innovation Campus.
reason: Sentences 457 and 459 describe a separate annual funding commitment, with a defined formula and duration, for a community fund tied to the Innovation Campus.

organization: the elected representatives who made up the Community Advisory Committee
claim: The Board urges the elected representatives who made up the Community Advisory Committee to monitor carefully the implementation of Resorts World’s Innovation Campus commitment.
reason: Sentence 461 is only an exhortation that elected representatives monitor implementation, not a concrete project obligation or condition.

claim: Resorts World commits to up to $5 million per year for the continuation of its Resorts World Gives program, with $25 million upfront.
reason: Sentence 462 states a concrete Resorts World commitment of up to $5 million per year plus $25 million upfront for the program.

claim: Resorts World commits to various mass transit improvements.
reason: Sentence 463 says Resorts World commits to mass transit improvements; although not detailed, it is still presented as a project commitment.
adjudicated_wording: Resorts World commits to various mass transit improvements.

claim: Resorts World commits to an open greenway and parks system providing ten acres of new open space on the casino’s campus.
reason: Sentence 463 commits to an open greenway and parks system with a measurable outcome: ten acres of new open space on campus.

claim: Resorts World commits to traffic infrastructure improvements.
reason: Sentence 463 expressly says Resorts World commits to traffic infrastructure improvements.
adjudicated_wording: Resorts World commits to traffic infrastructure improvements.

claim: Resorts World stated that it will conduct a Childcare Needs Assessment.
reason: Sentence 478 attributes to Resorts World a statement that it will conduct a Childcare Needs Assessment, which is a specific future action.

claim: Resorts World’s construction workforce diversity goals are 5 percent women, 40 percent minorities, and approximately 5 percent service-disabled veterans.
reason: Sentence 487 gives specific construction-workforce diversity goals attributable to Resorts World rather than an adopted mandate.

claim: The Board expects the service-disabled veterans’ permanent-employment target to be the required 6 percent rather than the 5 percent offered by Resorts World.
reason: Sentence 483 states the Board expects a 6 percent service-disabled-veterans target instead of 5 percent, which is a recommended stronger condition rather than an adopted term.
adjudicated_wording: The Board expects Resorts World's service-disabled veterans employment target to be the required 6 percent, rather than the 5 percent it offered.

claim: The Board expects the applicants’ stated goals and requirements regarding hiring local, diverse, and unionized workers to be met.
reason: Sentence 490 says the Board expects applicants’ stated hiring goals and requirements to be met; this is a board expectation tied to delivery, not an executed obligation in the text.
adjudicated_wording: The Board believes the Community Advisory Committee approvals were based on applicants’ representations about hiring local, diverse, and unionized workers, and it expects the applicants’ stated goals and requirements to be met.

organization: local elected officials, City and State agencies, community organizations, and the unions
claim: The Board urges local elected officials, City and State agencies, community organizations, and the unions to monitor carefully applicants’ hiring and procurement practices and to work with the applicants to ensure that the goals are met.
reason: Sentence 491 urges outside groups to monitor and work with applicants, but does not create a concrete project commitment or condition.

claim: Resorts World offered in its bid to pay the highest tax rate among the Applicants for its proposed casino, a term the Board says must remain unchanged and not be lowered to match other Applicants’ rates.
reason: Combines a factual bid term with the Board’s urging, but changes the modality to a term that “must remain unchanged”; the text only says the Board urges officials to resist lowering it.

organization: the Commission and elected officials at the state and local level
claim: The Board urges the Commission and elected officials at the state and local level to resist any back-tracking on the tax rate contained in Resorts World’s bid.
reason: Sentence 499 is a specific Board recommendation that officials resist any reduction in the tax rate in Resorts World’s bid.
adjudicated_wording: The Board urges the Commission and elected officials at the state and local level to resist any back-tracking on the tax rate contained in Resorts World’s bid.

claim: Resorts World committed to creating quality jobs as part of its proposed gaming facility development.
reason: The text explicitly refers to the applicant’s commitments to creating quality jobs.

claim: Resorts World committed to recruiting, training, and developing a diverse workforce.
reason: The text explicitly lists commitments to recruiting, training, and developing a diverse workforce.

claim: Resorts World committed to improving the transit and traffic infrastructure on the casino’s campus.
reason: The text explicitly lists commitments to improving transit and traffic infrastructure on the casino campus.

claim: Resorts World committed to building more open and park space into its campus.
reason: The text explicitly lists commitments to building more open and park space into the campus.

claim: The Board urges Resorts World to be more aggressive and concrete about local hiring and benefits for local businesses.
reason: It is a vague exhortation to be “more aggressive and concrete,” not a specific, trackable condition or commitment.

claim: The Board urges the Commission to use the license agreement to ensure acceptable quality if the casino opens while major construction is underway.
reason: Sentence 505 specifically urges the Commission to use the license agreement to ensure acceptable quality if opening occurs during major construction.
adjudicated_wording: The Gaming Facility Location Board recommends that the Commission use the license agreement to ensure acceptable quality if the casino opens while major construction is still underway.

claim: The selected Applicants are expected to act and perform with the utmost integrity, hold true to the commitments made to the community, and be accountable to the State and its residents and taxpayers.
reason: This is a broad expectation about integrity and accountability, not a concrete deliverable, target, or specific project duty.

claim: The Commission intends to move promptly to issue licenses so that construction can begin, jobs can be created, and revenues can be collected.
reason: It describes the Commission’s intended pace for the licensing review and issuance process, not a project deliverable.

claim: Resorts World New York City agreed to execute a monitoring agreement as set forth in the Commission's motion of December 15, 2025, as part of the basis for issuance of the Gaming Facility License Award.
reason: Sentence 15 makes RWNYC’s agreement to execute the monitoring agreement a concrete license-related obligation tied to issuance of the award.

claim: Resorts World New York City shall materially perform consistent with the content of its Application and commitments expressed during the Community Advisory Committee evaluative process, as determined or otherwise approved by the Commission.
reason: Sentence 56 imposes a binding condition to materially perform consistent with the Application and CAC commitments, subject to Commission approval/determination.

claim: Resorts World New York City shall pay, on or before December 31, 2025, a $500,000,000 gaming facility license fee by electronic funds transfer in accordance with Racing, Pari-Mutuel Wagering and Breeding Law § 1321-e(3) and 9 NYCRR § 601.1(b).
reason: Sentence 60 sets a specific, enforceable payment duty: $500,000,000 by December 31, 2025.

claim: Resorts World New York City shall, on or before December 31, 2025, deposit via cash or bond an amount representing 5 percent of the total investment proposed in the Application, in accordance with Racing, Pari-Mutuel Wagering and Breeding Law § 1321-e(1).
reason: Sentence 63 sets a specific, enforceable duty to deposit cash or bond equal to 5% of proposed total investment by December 31, 2025.

claim: Resorts World New York City shall establish milestones and budgets concerning the community benefits proposed in the Application and commitments expressed during the Community Advisory Committee evaluative process.
reason: Sentence 66 requires RWNYC to establish milestones and budgets for community benefits; that is a concrete accountability condition.

claim: Resorts World New York City shall post on its public website and submit to the Commission, for public dissemination without redaction, a community benefits progress report, including construction and operational workforce diversity and demographic data, at a frequency determined by the Commission.
reason: Sentence 67 requires public posting and Commission submission of community benefits progress reports, including workforce diversity and demographic data.

claim: Each community benefits progress report shall detail progress, set forth relevant budget and expenditure, and explain actual or anticipated delays in delivery of benefits proposed in the Application or Resorts World New York City's other commitments.
reason: Sentence 68 prescribes required contents of each community benefits progress report, creating a concrete reporting obligation.

claim: Resorts World New York City shall commence gaming operations promptly upon the Commission's determination that the permanent casino area of the Gaming Facility has been completed in accordance with the Application, Article 13 of the Racing, Pari-Mutuel Wagering and Breeding Law, and 9 NYCRR Part 5301.
reason: Sentence 71 requires RWNYC to commence gaming operations promptly once the Commission determines the permanent casino area is completed as required.

claim: Resorts World New York City shall comply in all material respects with third-party agreements included and/or proposed within the Application.
reason: Sentence 73 binds RWNYC to comply in all material respects with third-party agreements included or proposed in the Application.

claim: Resorts World New York City shall comply in all material respects with the Federal and State laws and regulations relating to its Gaming Facility.
reason: Sentence 76 is a general obligation to obey applicable federal and state law, without a distinct project deliverable or special public-benefit term.

organization: Resorts World New York City and its Commission-approved successors and assigns
claim: All of the terms and conditions of the License shall be binding upon Resorts World New York City and its Commission-approved successors and assigns.
reason: Sentence 84 makes all license terms binding on RWNYC and Commission-approved successors and assigns, a concrete accountability condition.
adjudicated_wording: All terms and conditions of the License are binding on Resorts World New York City and its Commission-approved successors and assigns.

organization: The Commission and Resorts World New York City
claim: The Commission and Resorts World New York City have a mutual intent to establish a third-party independent Compliance Monitoring Team in connection with this License to maintain financial integrity, enhance compliance and ethics programs, establish policies and procedures, prevent money laundering, and ensure the delivery of promised public benefits.
reason: Sentence 87 states only a 'mutual intent' to establish a Compliance Monitoring Team; within the target window it does not itself clearly impose the operative obligation.

claim: Resorts World New York City shall promptly contract with, and compensate appropriately, an independent third-party Compliance Monitoring Team firm, proposed by Resorts World New York City and approved by the Commission, to monitor and report to the Commission, with notice to Resorts World New York City’s board of directors, as frequently as the Commission may request, on Resorts World New York City’s ongoing compliance with each element of the Application and its regulatory obligations, with the specifics and scope of reporting to be approved by the Commission and updated from time to time thereafter.
reason: Sentence 88 imposes an adopted license duty on Resorts World New York City to promptly hire and pay an approved independent CMT firm and have it monitor/report compliance to the Commission.

claim: Under the required Compliance Monitoring Team arrangement, Resorts World New York City’s compliance reporting must cover anti-money laundering compliance, including Know Your Customer, Suspicious Activity Report, and Currency Transition Report compliance.
reason: Sentences 88 and 90 make AML/KYC/SAR/CTR coverage a required topic within the mandated CMT monitoring and reporting.

claim: Under the required Compliance Monitoring Team arrangement, Resorts World New York City’s compliance reporting must cover Commission regulatory requirements.
reason: Sentences 88 and 92 require the CMT reporting to cover Commission regulatory requirements.

claim: Under the required Compliance Monitoring Team arrangement, Resorts World New York City’s compliance reporting must cover the community benefits proposed in the Application and the commitments expressed during the Community Advisory Committee evaluative process, including completion or delivery milestones.
reason: Sentences 88 and 94 require the CMT reporting to cover application community benefits and CAC commitments, including delivery milestones.

claim: Under the required Compliance Monitoring Team arrangement, Resorts World New York City’s compliance reporting must cover compliance with any restrictions or requirements the Commission has set forth.
reason: Sentences 88 and 96 require the CMT reporting to cover compliance with Commission-set restrictions or requirements.

claim: The Compliance Monitoring Team firm engaged for this License shall be independent of Resorts World New York City’s auditors, legal counsel, and consultants for a minimum of five years prior to the engagement.
reason: Sentence 97 sets a concrete eligibility restriction for the engaged CMT firm: independence from RWNYC's auditors, counsel, and consultants for at least five years before engagement.

claim: The contract between Resorts World New York City and the Compliance Monitoring Team shall be subject to the Commission’s prior approval, Resorts World New York City may not terminate that contract unilaterally or otherwise without the Commission’s prior written approval, and Resorts World New York City shall terminate the contract if directed by the Commission.
reason: Sentence 98 imposes concrete Commission-control terms on the CMT contract: prior approval, no termination without prior written approval, and termination if the Commission directs it.
